variants.headline: Party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by a party leader.
variants.body:
A party leader has blundered in an election debate. The misstep is established, but the words involved and their effect on voters are not supplied here. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the debate event from a fabricated quotation or a claim that the election's outcome has been decided.

Workers deserve political debate about the conditions of their lives, not merely a competition in speaking neatly. A leader's blunder can deserve attention without displacing wages, safety and services from the argument. Labour should keep the standard practical and refuse to make a performance the whole measure of representation.

We criticise {target} in this assessment. Political leadership includes judgment under scrutiny, and a debate blunder is an appropriate occasion to question whether the standard of public presentation has been adequate. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
